dek.text: Two judges recommend approving El Paso Electric's gas plant for Meta's data center only if its other customers are held harmless for its life.

introduction.text: [El Paso Electric asked the Public Utility Commission to amend its certificate so it can build a {{number:c1}} MW natural gas plant called the McCloud facility](c1). [It would primarily serve a data center that Wurldwide is developing in El Paso County](c1). [Wurldwide is owned by Meta Platforms](c2), the proposal for decision notes, citing the utility's own application. [The plant would be {{number:c6}} modular gas generators rated at {{number:c6:1}} kilowatts each](c6), [on approximately {{number:c8}} acres immediately adjacent to the data center](c8).

[Two administrative law judges heard the case by videoconference on {{date:c39}}](c39). [Their proposal for decision was filed in the docket on {{date:c38}}](c38). [They recommend approval only if El Paso Electric holds its customers other than Wurldwide harmless from the plant's costs](c28). [Without that condition they would recommend denial](c29).

sections.heading: Who pays, and for how long

paragraphs.text: [El Paso Electric proposes a bridge period of up to five years in which Wurldwide takes all of the plant's output and carries all of its capital costs](c23). [Its witness James Schichtl testified that the bridge lasts as long as it takes to extend transmission to the data center's site](c24). [After that the utility may fold McCloud into its generation resources and revise its rates, and no decision has been made](c25). [Any change in cost responsibility would need Commission approval in a separate case](c25). [It would not commit to Wurldwide being the only customer to pay the plant's costs after the bridge](c26).

[The utility estimates a {{number:c19}} year service life for the plant](c19). The judges' condition reaches all of it. [Their proposed ordering paragraph holds the other retail customers harmless from any capital or operating costs of the facility for its life](c30). [The condition lifts only if the utility later shows the plant meets the statute's test](c30). [They limited the condition to those capital and operating costs](c31).

[The judges found the utility showed a need for capacity to serve the data center but did not show McCloud is a cost-effective and reliable resource](c27). [They found the plant isn't needed to serve any other El Paso Electric customer](c51). [The utility engaged Enchanted Rock after Wurldwide preferred that vendor](c16). [It acknowledged it considered no alternative and issued no request for proposals](c17). [It ran no cost-benefit analysis for its ratepayers](c18). [McCloud would be the largest project Enchanted Rock has built and the utility's first experience with modular gas generation](c52).

[The data center has committed to a peak demand of {{number:c12}} MW by the end of {{number:c12:1}}](c12). [The judges found the utility can serve about the first {{number:c13}} MW of that load from its existing resources](c13). [The second block of about {{number:c13:2}} MW requires additional capacity](c13).

[The judges' proposed findings put the plant's total estimated cost at approximately {{money:c20}}](c20). [That estimate covers the generation facilities only and excludes transmission interconnection](c21). [Per kilowatt the plant costs $1,609 against $1,264 for a generic gas combustion turbine in the utility's own resource plan](c56). [The City of El Paso asked for a capital cost cap of $565.6 million](c22). [The judges declined the cap and a performance guarantee and said the hold-harmless condition already protects customers from the plant's costs](c55).

[The Commission will place the case on an open meeting agenda and notify the parties of the date](c37). [KVIA reports that the five commissioners will decide whether to accept, change or reject the recommendation, and that a final order is expected by {{date:c42}}](c42). [On Monday El Paso City Council authorized a counteroffer for a full hold harmless](c46). [El Paso Electric's chief executive Kelly Tomblin told KVIA the utility is not seeking to shift those costs onto residential or other customers](c48).

The docket is public on the PUCT Interchange. [It holds comments from {{number:c45}} protestors filed by the Sembrando Esperanza Coalition](c45), and [residents have filed comments of their own](c44).

The proposal for decision is a recommendation and not a ruling. It names no payer for the plant's costs after the bridge if the commissioners drop the condition. [The cost estimate carries no transmission interconnection cost for the day the plant joins the utility's system](c21). [The judges also left the cost of serving the data center's first load outside this case](c49).
